concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
question: The elements that are liquid at room temperature (25°C) are:
solution:
The correct answer is __**bromine and mercury**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bromine (Br)** and **mercury (Hg)** are the only two elements that are liquid at room temperature (25ºC).
 
• **Bromine** is a reddish-brown liquid and is the only non-metallic element that is liquid at room temperature.
 
• **Mercury** is a silvery liquid metal, known for its unique property of being liquid at room temperature.
 
• Both elements have significant industrial and scientific applications due to their unique physical properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Melting and Boiling Points:** Bromine melts at -7.2°C and boils at 58.8°C, while mercury melts at -38.83°C and boils at 356.7°C.
 
• **Density:** Bromine has a density of 3.1028 g/cm³, and mercury has a density of 13.534 g/cm³, making it one of the densest liquids.
 
• **Toxicity:** Both bromine and mercury are toxic and require careful handling. Mercury exposure can lead to mercury poisoning, while bromine can cause burns and respiratory issues.
 
• **Uses of Bromine:** Bromine is used in flame retardants, water purification, and as a reactant in organic synthesis.
 
• **Uses of Mercury:** Mercury is used in thermometers, barometers, fluorescent lamps, and amalgams for dental fillings, though its use has decreased due to toxicity concerns.
